entities.summary:
United Airlines Flight 175 was a commercial airliner hijacked by terrorists on September 11, 2001. The Boeing 767 aircraft, registered as N612UA, was flying from Boston's Logan International Airport to Los Angeles International Airport when it crashed into the South Tower of the World Trade Center in New York City. The impact and subsequent fire caused significant damage to the tower, resulting in the deaths of 658 people. The event was a pivotal moment in modern history, marking a turning point in the War on Terror.

The hijacking was orchestrated by a group of terrorists affiliated with al-Qaeda, led by Mohamed Atta. Atta, a 33-year-old Egyptian national, had been planning the attacks for months, recruiting and training a team of operatives to carry out the mission. The group's goal was to inflict maximum damage on the United States, targeting iconic symbols of American power and influence.

In the aftermath of the 9/11 attacks, the United States launched the War on Terror, a global military campaign aimed at defeating al-Qaeda and its affiliates. The conflict would go on to span multiple continents, resulting in the deaths of thousands of civilians and the displacement of millions more. The legacy of the 9/11 attacks continues to shape global politics and international relations to this day.

As the world remembers the victims of that fateful day, it is a sobering reminder of the devastating consequences of terrorism and the importance of continued vigilance in the face of evolving threats.
